questions.question: How was the way of life of the first farmers different from that of the San hunter-gatherers?
questions.expected_answer: The San got all their food from the wild and moved with the seasons. The first farmers grew crops such as sorghum, millet, beans and pumpkins, kept cattle, sheep and goats, and lived in settled villages. Farming produced more food from less land, and grain could be stored.

questions.question: Explain how the first farmers came to southern Africa and how historians know about it.
questions.expected_answer: Their ancestors lived in West and Central Africa and spread south and east very slowly, family by family, over many generations, reaching Limpopo, Mpumalanga and KwaZulu-Natal by about 1,800 years ago. Historians know this from archaeology, such as pottery, iron tools, slag, burnt seeds, cattle bones and house floors, and from how related languages spread.

questions.question: Describe how the first farmers made iron and why iron tools were important.
questions.expected_answer: They put charcoal and crushed iron ore in a clay furnace and pumped in air with skin bellows to make it very hot, so the iron separated from the rock. A smith heated and hammered the iron into tools. Iron hoes, axes, spears and knives were stronger and lasted longer than stone tools, making farming and clearing land easier.
